q: Hudson Hardware has assets of $80,000 and liabilities of $30,000. What is the owner's equity?
r: Equity equals assets minus liabilities: 80,000 - 30,000.
w: This is the amount of liabilities.
This is the amount of assets.

q: Which type of account normally has a debit balance?
r: Asset
Assets increase with debits, so their normal balance is a debit.
w: Revenue accounts normally have credit balances.
Equity accounts normally have credit balances.

q: Which of the following is an asset of a business?
r: Equipment the business owns
Assets are resources owned that have value to the business.
w: This is an amount the business owes.
This is an obligation to provide goods or services later.
An expense is a cost of operating, not something owned.

q: A business buys office supplies for cash. How does this transaction affect the accounting equation?
r: One asset increases and another asset decreases by the same amount
Supplies go up and cash goes down, so total assets do not change.
w: Nothing was owed or paid off.
One asset replaced another of the same value.

q: In double-entry accounting, what must be true for every transaction?
r: Total debits equal total credits
Every transaction affects at least two accounts and stays balanced.
w: Debits are always larger than credits
Double-entry affects at least two accounts.

q: What does GAAP stand for in accounting?
r: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
GAAP is the common set of rules used to prepare financial statements.
w: This is not the standard name.
GAAP is not government approved policy.
This is not what GAAP stands for.

q: Which principle requires a business's records to be kept separate from its owner's personal finances?
r: Business entity concept
The business is treated as its own unit for record keeping.
w: This assumes the business will keep operating.
This pairs expenses with the revenue they help earn.
This records assets at their original cost.

q: A company records a delivery truck at its $42,000 purchase price even though it could now sell for more. Which principle is being followed?
r: Cost principle
Assets are recorded at what was paid for them.
w: This covers when revenue is recorded.
This lets small items be handled simply.

q: Why do public companies have their financial statements audited by independent CPAs?
r: To give users confidence the statements are fairly presented
An independent opinion adds credibility for investors and lenders.
w: To prepare the company's tax return
Tax preparation is a separate service.
To set the company's stock price
To replace the company's accounting staff
Auditors review records; they do not replace the accounting staff.

q: Which law was passed to improve the accuracy of corporate financial reporting after major accounting scandals?
r: Sarbanes-Oxley Act
It set stricter rules for financial reporting and audits.
w: This law covers wages and hours.
This created the Social Security program.

q: Which source document is created when a business sells goods to a customer?
r: Sales invoice
An invoice records what was sold, to whom and for how much.
w: This is sent by a buyer to order goods.
The bank issues this to show account activity.

q: A business receives cash from a customer for services performed. Which journal entry is correct?
r: Debit Cash and credit Service Revenue
Cash increases with a debit and revenue increases with a credit.
w: Debit Service Revenue and credit Cash
Debit Accounts Payable and credit Cash
This would pay off a bill.
Debit Cash and credit Accounts Payable
This would record a new debt.

q: What is posting in the accounting cycle?
r: Transferring journal entries to ledger accounts
Posting updates each account's balance.

q: What is the main purpose of a trial balance?
r: To check that total debits equal total credits
It helps find posting errors before statements are prepared.
w: To report the period's net income
This is the job of the income statement.
To list all customers who owe money

q: At the end of a period, which entry records an expense that has been incurred but not yet paid?
r: Adjusting entry
Adjusting entries bring accounts up to date before statements are prepared.
w: Closing entries transfer temporary account balances to equity.
An opening entry sets up the books at the start.

q: What does accounts receivable represent?
r: Money owed to the business by its customers
Receivables arise when sales are made on credit.
w: Money the business owes its suppliers
Cash held in the business's bank account
The value of the owner's investment

q: Why does a business set up an allowance for doubtful accounts?
r: To estimate receivables that will not be collected
The allowance matches expected bad debts to the period's sales.
w: To list the accounts a business plans to buy
To increase the balance of accounts receivable
The allowance reduces the net receivable.

q: An invoice carries terms of 2/10, n/30. What do these terms mean?
r: A 2 percent discount if paid within 10 days; the full amount is due in 30 days
The buyer earns a discount for paying early.
w: A 10 percent discount if paid within 2 days
A $2 fee if paid after 10 days
The terms describe a discount, not a fee.
The invoice is due in 2 days or 10 days
Terms describe discount and full-payment periods.

q: A $2,000 invoice has terms of 2/10, n/30. How much is paid if the buyer pays on day 8?
r: The 2 percent discount is $40, leaving $1,960.
w: This adds the discount instead of subtracting it.

q: How is an unpaid bill from a supplier recorded?
r: As accounts payable
Money owed to suppliers is a liability.
w: Receivables are owed to the business.
A bill owed is not revenue.
A supplier's bill is a debt, not equity.

q: Which payroll taxes are withheld from employees' paychecks and matched by the employer?
r: Social Security and Medicare taxes
These FICA taxes are shared by employee and employer.
w: This is paid on real estate.
This applies to the property of someone who has died.

q: A store collects sales tax from customers. How is the collected tax recorded until it is paid to the government?
r: As a liability
The store holds the money for the government.
w: Collected tax is not the store's income.
The store does not bear the cost of the tax.
As an asset of the owner
The money is owed to the government.

q: Which form reports an employee's yearly wages and the taxes withheld?
r: Form W-2
Employers send it to employees and the government after year end.
w: Employees use it to set withholding.

q: Which action is a legal way to reduce a business's tax bill?
r: Claiming the deductions and credits the law allows
Tax planning within the rules is legal.
w: Leaving some income out of the return
Failing to file breaks the law.

q: What does a tax deduction reduce?
r: Taxable income
Deductions lower the income that tax is calculated on.
w: The tax bill dollar for dollar
Deductions apply to the taxpayer's income.

q: Which financial statement shows what a business owns and what it owes on a specific date?
r: Balance sheet
It lists assets, liabilities and owner's equity.
w: This shows revenue and expenses over a period.
This tracks cash inflows and outflows.
This checks that debits equal credits.

q: How is net income calculated?
r: Revenue minus expenses
Net income is what remains after all expenses are deducted.
w: Adding them does not give income.

q: Which item appears on an income statement?
r: Service revenue
Revenues and expenses are reported on the income statement.
w: This is a balance sheet liability.
This is part of equity on the balance sheet.
This is a balance sheet asset.

q: Hudson Hardware had revenues of $120,000 and expenses of $95,000. The owner withdrew $10,000 and began the year with $60,000 in equity. What is the ending equity?
r: 60,000 + 25,000 net income - 10,000 withdrawals.
w: This adds the withdrawals instead of subtracting them.
This is only the net income.

q: Which of the following is a current asset?
r: Cash
Current assets are cash and items expected to become cash within a year.
w: A building is a long-term asset.
A truck is a long-term asset.

q: Which spreadsheet formula adds the values in cells A1 through A10?
r: =SUM(A1:A10)
SUM totals a range of cells.
w: This is not a valid formula.
This is not a valid formula.

q: What is a main benefit of cloud-based accounting software?
r: Authorized users can reach the records from anywhere with an internet connection
Records are stored online rather than on a single computer.
w: It removes the need for any security
It works only on one computer
That is the opposite of cloud access.

q: Which control best prevents unauthorized changes to electronic accounting records?
r: Individual logins with role-based permissions
Unique access lets the business limit and track changes.
w: Shared passwords hide who made a change.
Leaving the system open on a public computer
This makes access easy to steal.

q: Accounting software refuses to post an entry where debits do not equal credits. What type of control is this?
r: An automated control
The system checks and blocks the error automatically.
w: No person is reviewing the entry.
An audit is done by outside examiners.

q: Backing up accounting data protects a business against:
r: Loss of records
A backup lets the business restore its data.
w: Backups do not affect interest rates.
Backups do not affect tax rules.

q: Which credential is held by an accountant who has passed a licensing exam and met state requirements?
r: Certified Public Accountant
The CPA is the standard license for public accounting.
w: This is a degree, not a license.
This focuses on personal financial planning.

q: Which professional examines financial records to decide whether statements are fairly presented?
r: Auditor
Auditors review records and give an opinion on the statements.
w: Payroll clerks prepare pay and deductions.

q: Which skill is most important for an accountant?
r: Attention to detail
Small errors can affect the accuracy of financial reports.
w: This is not central to accounting.

q: Which task is typically done by a bookkeeper?
r: Recording daily financial transactions
Bookkeepers keep the day-to-day records.

q: What do forensic accountants mainly do?
r: Investigate financial records for fraud
They trace money and examine evidence in disputes.
